items.followUp: Write down any four properties of a colloidal solution.

rubric.why: Identifies a suspension as heterogeneous and/or describes its particles settling.
rubric.description: State that a suspension is heterogeneous or that its particles settle on standing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct property.

rubric.why: Suspension particles are large enough to be seen.
rubric.description: State that suspension particles are large or visible to the naked eye.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct statement.

rubric.why: Suspension particles can be separated from the mixture by filtration.
rubric.description: State that suspension particles can be separated by filtration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct separation property.

rubric.why: Suspensions scatter light because of their dispersed particles.
rubric.description: State that a suspension scatters light or is opaque.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct property.

modelAnswer: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
Its particles are large enough to be seen with the naked eye.
The particles settle down when the suspension is left standing.
The particles can be separated from the mixture by filtration.

items.followUp: Explain how a covalent bond can split to form free radicals.

rubric.why: Names the equal splitting of a covalent bond as homolytic fission or cleavage.
rubric.description: State that free radicals form by homolytic fission of a covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the bond splitting process.

rubric.why: Each atom receives one electron from the shared pair, leaving an unpaired electron.
rubric.description: Explain that each atom takes one bonding electron and becomes a radical with an unpaired electron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct electron distribution.

modelAnswer: Free radicals are formed by the homolytic fission of a covalent bond.
The shared pair of electrons divides equally, so each atom takes one electron and has an unpaired electron.

items.followUp: Explain why the first ionization energy of potassium is lower than that of calcium.

rubric.why: Sodium has one electron in its outer 3s subshell, whereas magnesium has two.
rubric.description: Compare the outer-electron configurations of sodium and magnesium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying sodium's outer electron or the relevant configurations.

rubric.why: Magnesium has a greater nuclear charge and smaller atomic radius, so it attracts its outer electron more strongly.
rubric.description: Explain that magnesium holds its outer electron more strongly, making its ionization energy higher.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct comparison of attraction or ionization energy.

modelAnswer: Sodium has the electronic configuration 2,8,1, while magnesium has 2,8,2.
Magnesium has a greater nuclear charge and a smaller atomic radius, so its outer electrons are held more strongly; therefore, sodium has the lower ionization energy.

items.followUp: Define an ionic bond and give one example.

rubric.why: A chemical bond is the force that holds atoms or ions together in a substance.
rubric.description: Give a correct definition of a chemical bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining attractive force or holding-together idea.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates the definition.
rubric.description: Give one correct example of a substance with a chemical bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: A chemical bond is the attractive force that holds atoms or ions together in a molecule or compound.
For example, the hydrogen atoms in H₂ are held together by a chemical bond.

items.followUp: Show, using electron configurations, how Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions are formed.

rubric.why: A sodium atom loses one electron to form a positively charged sodium ion.
rubric.description: Explain the formation of Na⁺ by loss of one electron from sodium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct electron loss and resulting ion.

rubric.why: A chlorine atom gains one electron to form a negatively charged chloride ion.
rubric.description: Explain the formation of Cl⁻ by gain of one electron by chlorine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct electron gain and resulting ion.

modelAnswer: A sodium atom loses one electron to form a sodium ion: Na → Na⁺ + e⁻.
A chlorine atom gains that electron to form a chloride ion: Cl + e⁻ → Cl⁻.

items.followUp: Explain why a water molecule is polar.

rubric.why: The greater electronegativity of chlorine makes the sharing of the bonding electrons unequal.
rubric.description: State that chlorine attracts the shared electrons more strongly than hydrogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying unequal sharing or the electronegativity difference.

rubric.why: Unequal sharing produces partial charges and a dipole, making HCl polar.
rubric.description: State that partial charges or a dipole form, so the molecule is polar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the consequence of unequal sharing.

modelAnswer: Chlorine is more electronegative than hydrogen, so the shared electron pair in HCl is attracted more towards chlorine.
This creates partial charges, Hδ⁺ and Clδ⁻, and a dipole; therefore, HCl is a polar molecule.

items.followUp: Define diffusion of gases and give an example involving ammonia and hydrogen chloride.

accept: movement from higher concentration to lower concentration
rubric.why: Diffusion is the net spreading of gas particles from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration.
rubric.description: Define diffusion of gases in terms of particle movement and concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: A suitable example demonstrates gases spreading and mixing.
rubric.description: Give a correct example of diffusion of gases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an appropriate example.

modelAnswer: Diffusion of gases is the spreading and mixing of gas particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
For example, the smell of perfume spreads through a room by diffusion.

items.followUp: Why are gases less dense than liquids?

rubric.why: Particles in solids are packed more closely than particles in liquids.
rubric.description: Compare the spacing or packing of particles in solids and liquids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that solid particles are more closely packed.

rubric.why: Closer packing means a given volume of solid generally contains more mass, giving it greater density.
rubric.description: Link close packing to greater mass per unit volume or greater density.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct density consequence.

modelAnswer: The particles in solids are packed more closely together than those in liquids, with less empty space between them.
Therefore, a given volume of a solid generally contains more mass and has a greater density.
